title: ACLs as Security: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Picture a members only club. The guard checks the rules in order. The most specific rules must come first.

scenes.heading: The club rules
scenes.narration: A few facts drive every access list. Rules are checked top down, and the first match wins. Everything not allowed is blocked by the implicit deny. Standard lists go near the destination. Extended lists go near the source.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. Extended lists match ports and protocols too. Inbound lists don't filter traffic the router creates. The implicit deny is always present.

items.right: Extended can match ports and protocols

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva ACL security lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Specific rules go first. Standard near destination, extended near source. The implicit deny is always there. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva ACL security lab.

points.t: Standard: near destination. Extended: near source
